result.summary:
All five code removals (R1-R5) and all five companion design edits (C1-C5) applied exactly as the design specifies; two files changed, nothing else. `git diff --stat`: `lib/letflow/design/iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md | 62 +++++++++++--` and `lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex | 11 +---`, 2 files changed, 60 insertions(+), 13 deletions(-). No test file was touched -- RT-9 is left for TEST-DESIGNER at Step 4 per design §8 item 7.

CODE DIFF, R-number by R-number (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex): R1 -- deleted `owner_pid: pid(),` from @typep provision_op (was :160), leaving from/owner_ref/sandbox_id/schema_name/owner_down?. R2 -- deleted `owner_pid: owner_pid,` from reserve_slot/2's {:provision, %{...}} literal (was :535); the local `owner_pid = elem(from, 0)` (:527) and `owner_ref = Process.monitor(owner_pid)` (:528) are byte-for-byte untouched, confirmed both by the diff (neither line appears in it) and by the clean compile. R3 -- deleted `#                  schema_name: String.t()` from the in_flight: block of the state-shape comment (was :316) and dropped the trailing comma from the preceding `#                  task_pid:    pid(),`. R4 -- deleted `schema_name: op_schema_name(op)` from pump/1's in_flight literal (was :572) and dropped the trailing comma from `task_pid: task.pid,`. R5 -- deleted both clause heads of `defp op_schema_name/1` (was :592-593) and the blank line that followed them. `owner_ref` is untouched everywhere; no accessor helper was added; no rename, reorder or extra typespec was introduced.

DESIGN DIFF, C-number by C-number (lib/letflow/design/iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md): C1 -- §5's provision_op() block, `  owner_pid:   pid(),` (:502) replaced IN PLACE by `  # owner_pid REMOVED by ISS-0227 (2026-08-22) -- write-only; derive as elem(p.from, 0). See §17.`; the surviving five fields are neither reordered nor renumbered. C2 -- §5's in_flight() block, `  schema_name: String.t()` (:521) replaced IN PLACE by the two-line removal marker naming the derivation from in_flight.op, and the trailing comma dropped from `  task_pid:    pid(),` (:520) so op/task_ref/task_pid form a well-formed map. C3 -- §7 step 2, :804's enumerated literal now reads `{:provision, %{from:, owner_ref:, sandbox_id:, schema_name:, owner_down?: false}}` and is immediately followed by the added line `**`owner_pid` was removed from this literal by ISS-0227 (2026-08-22)** — see §17.`; :802's prose about the two surviving LOCAL bindings is unchanged, as §5.4 requires. C4 -- new `## 17. Extension (ISS-0227, 2026-08-22) — two write-only fields removed` appended after the former last line (:1902), following precedent 2's heading shape, carrying all five required contents: the removal and its authority (naming iss0227-sandbox-pool-dead-field-removal.md), the two derivations with their equivalence arguments, op_schema_name/1's removal and the measured warnings-as-errors reason, §6's explicit no-invariant-change statement enumerating INV-SP-A1..A7 / INV-SP-1..7 / DOWN-1..5 / T1..T5 plus the owner-monitor and no-external-behaviour-change statements, and a pointer back to C1/C2/C3's in-place markers. C5 -- the dated ISS-0227 blockquote pointer inserted immediately after the Status line (:4), BEFORE the round-1 REWORK NOTICE blockquote. Nothing in §5.7's do-not-edit list was changed: no INV-SP-* statement, no §7 step 3 clause A/B or case 4b, no §10 RT contract, no §11/§13/§14/§15/§16, neither REWORK NOTICE, no F-/R2-F- row, and §12's file table.

FOUR CHECKS, REAL OUTPUT:

(1) `mix format --check-formatted` -> no output, `EXIT=0`.

(2) `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> `EXIT=0`. Full dependency tree compiled from cold (mime, plug_crypto, hpax, jose, decimal, jason, telemetry_registry, oidcc, thousand_island, db_connection, ecto, plug, ueberauth, ueberauth_oidcc, postgrex, ecto_sql, websock, bandit), ending `==> letflow / Compiling 104 files (.ex) / Generated letflow app / EXIT=0`. NO `function op_schema_name/1 is unused` warning (so R5 was not skipped) and NO undefined-variable report at :528 (so the :527 local was not deleted in error). The only warnings printed were pre-existing and not from letflow's own sources: jose's 22 Erlang `'catch ...' is deprecated` warnings from src/jwa/jose_jwa.erl and src/jose_server.erl, and a Mix-level `"xref: [exclude: ...]" in your mix.exs file is deprecated` notice emitted while compiling the ueberauth_oidcc dependency. Neither category is a letflow compiler warning and neither affected the exit code, which was 0.

(3) `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs test/letflow/sandbox_pool_call_timeout_test.exs test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs` -> `Finished in 65.1 seconds (0.00s async, 65.1s sync)` / `Result: 32 passed`. Zero failures, zero skipped, zero invalid; seed 866464, max_cases 32. The 32 decomposes as 16 (sandbox_pool_test.exs) + 4 (sandbox_pool_call_timeout_test.exs) = the stated 20-passed baseline for the first two files, unchanged, plus 12 (promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs). This matches design §4's finding that no existing test reads either removed field. Ran against LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5472 from the worktree's own .env; the run's own log lines confirm it saw the sibling workspace via application_name and deferred TenantSchemaReaper's orphan sweep rather than reaping across workspaces.

(4) GH #465 acceptance criterion 4, run code-file-restricted per design §4.1 / §12 (an unrestricted pattern trips on this repo's own design-doc prose -- docs/anti-patterns.md:1195): `git grep -nE "owner_pid:|schema_name: op_schema_name|op_schema_name" -- 'lib/**/*.ex' 'test/**/*.exs'` -> NO OUTPUT, `EXIT=1`. Exactly the post-fix result §12 predicts. The pre-fix control, same command against the branch's starting commit -- `git grep -nE "owner_pid:|schema_name: op_schema_name|op_schema_name" 233af04 -- 'lib/**/*.ex' 'test/**/*.exs'` -> `EXIT=0` with exactly the five removal-set lines and nothing else: `233af04:lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex:160:           owner_pid: pid(),`, `:535:         owner_pid: owner_pid,`, `:572:          schema_name: op_schema_name(op)`, `:592:  defp op_schema_name({:provision, %{schema_name: schema_name}}), do: schema_name`, `:593:  defp op_schema_name({:drop, %{schema_name: schema_name}}), do: schema_name`. Five before, zero after -- R1, R2, R4 and R5 are each accounted for by a line that was there and is not now. (R3 is a comment-only edit and is by design not matched by this pattern; it is visible in the diff.)

Nothing in the design could not be executed as written. Every line citation in §2 and §5 landed on exactly the content the design said it would, at exactly the stated line numbers. All four checks were run synchronously in this turn as foreground blocking calls, with no backgrounding and no wakeup expectation, per core-directives.md's No Background Wait rule.
